sources.title: SQLite isolation
sources.declared_version: SQLite official living documentation; WAL supported since 3.7.0 (2010-07-21)
sources.inspected_scope: Separate-connection isolation; WAL read transactions; rollback mode; shared-cache/read_uncommitted exception
sources.independent_finding: WAL read transactions retain their read view; independent page transactions do not. Shared cache plus read_uncommitted is a specific exception. Database isolation does not freeze external blobs.

sources.title: SQLite Online Backup API
sources.independent_observed_version_or_context: SQLite living backup documentation, page update 2025-11-13
sources.inspected_scope: Overview and section 3.1, checked against C interface
sources.independent_finding: Incremental copying releases source locks. Other-connection writes can restart the copy; repeated restarts can prevent completion. A successful result is consistent, but an unpinned initial start-time identity must not be inferred after restarts.

sources.title: PostgreSQL transaction isolation
sources.independent_finding: The stable snapshot begins at the first non-transaction-control statement. Read-only Repeatable Read does not need serialization-conflict retries; a stable view is not a claim of serializable business-rule consistency.

sources.title: RFC 8259 JSON
sources.independent_finding: UTF-8 exchange, SHOULD-unique keys, integer interoperability limits and parser limits are supported. Rejecting duplicate keys is an application policy. NDJSON is not specified here.

sources.title: RFC 3339 timestamps
sources.declared_version: RFC 3339, July 2002; RFC Editor says updated by RFC 9557
sources.independent_finding: The final repeats the original 3339 distinction between -00:00 and Z while acknowledging an update in its source map. The governing 9557 update gives Z and -00:00 the same unknown-local-offset meaning; +00:00 remains distinct. See C01.

sources.title: PKWARE ZIP APPNOTE
sources.independent_finding: Descriptors permit streaming; ZIP64 expands size/count/offset representations; each member has central-directory metadata. Structural close does not prove application completeness, authenticity, or an OS reader matrix.

sources.title: GNU tar manual
sources.independent_observed_version_or_context: Retrieved living GNU tar manual: 1.35.90, 11 June 2026
sources.independent_finding: PAX/ustar comparisons are supported. The frozen source map labels this living URL as GNU tar 1.35; the retrieved edition is different. The final explicitly caveats its predecessor retrieval limits. See C03.

sources.title: GitLab export docs
sources.declared_version: GitLab living docs accessed 2026-10-12, not version-pinned
sources.inspected_scope: Backup warning; user mapping; NDJSON; compatibility; version-dependent item inventory
sources.independent_finding: An explicit warning against using project exports as backups is present. Item scope and user mapping depend on GitLab version and roles. It is precedent, not the unknown tracker contract.

sources.title: GitLab project export schema
sources.declared_version: GitLab 19.2 stable EE branch head, commit fc45538465514c4777fc196641900b63470c6236
sources.inspected_scope: CE/EE relation tree, included/excluded attributes, custom_attributes, issues, import_only_tree
sources.independent_finding: The explicit domain allowlist and compatibility-only associations are real. This commit is independently verified; the branch-head label is not independently attested by a historical branch capture.

sources.title: GitLab project TreeSaver
sources.independent_finding: Current user and excluded relations reach the serializer; writer close is in ensure; Net::OpenTimeout retries are present. This code does not itself establish a global snapshot.

sources.title: GitLab StreamingSerializer
sources.inspected_scope: StreamingSerializer execute, batching, authorization, rescue and callbacks
sources.independent_finding: BATCH_SIZE=100, keyset/configured ordering, restricted-association authorization and a log-and-skip relation-batch rescue are verified. Callbacks and replica use preclude inferring generic source immutability from this precedent.

sources.title: GitLab ExportService
sources.inspected_scope: ExportService authorization, component savers, archive saver, error path and ensure cleanup
sources.independent_finding: Authorization and separate data/blob/repository savers, archive orchestration and cleanup are supported. This application-specific orchestration is not evidence that the proposed tracker exporter has been built or is read-only.

sources.title: GitLab ExportTask caller
sources.independent_finding: The task checks project and destination directory, calls ExportService with a move strategy, and disables object storage for that path. It is a caller example, not a guarantee for every destination.

sources.title: GitLab NDJSON writer
sources.independent_finding: Array relations are emitted one JSON value and newline at a time; file mode is append. The final appropriately treats this as an application convention.

sources.title: GitLab TreeSaver tests
sources.independent_finding: Relevant intended field and relationship assertions are present. Neither candidate nor evaluator ran this suite.

sources.title: GitLab NDJSON writer tests
sources.independent_finding: Root, relation append and write/read assertions are present. Source inspection is not executed validation or a complete fidelity test.

sources.title: GitLab EE permission tests
sources.inspected_scope: EE TreeSaver tests: epic unreadability and denied note association
sources.independent_finding: An inaccessible epic is omitted; denying one note leaves the other two. These are GitLab-specific test definitions, not proof of the unknown tracker authorization policy.

sources.title: NIST Secure Hash Standard
sources.declared_version: FIPS 180-4 final 2015-08-04; revision planned per NIST page
sources.inspected_scope: NIST publication abstract and planning note
sources.independent_finding: Digest-based change detection is supported. An editable manifest does not authenticate the producer.

sources.title: OWASP archive security test guide
sources.declared_version: OWASP WSTG latest living page, version not pinned
sources.independent_finding: Extraction and later processing can cross directory boundaries or exhaust resources. These threats support importer limits; they do not require content-addressed exporter paths.

sources.title: GitLab large export issue
sources.declared_version: Reporter says self-managed GitLab 16.5.3 on Kubernetes; no fix status established in reviewed page
sources.inspected_scope: Issue body, reported export status, upload/destination symptoms and environment version
sources.independent_finding: The large-export report was accessible in the independent retrieval. The symptoms are reported observations; no root cause or current fix was established. Candidate retrieval failure is not disproved by a different later transport succeeding.

sources.title: GitLab relation export MR
sources.declared_version: Merged MR, June 2022; release adoption not established
sources.independent_observed_version_or_context: Historical MR requested June 20, 2022; page edited July 19, 2022
sources.independent_finding: Independent web retrieval verifies staged per-relation exports, object-store upload and tarball assembly as a then-unused proposal. Terminal urllib returned HTTP 403. Current adoption is not asserted or established.

sources.title: GitLab direct-transfer release history
sources.independent_finding: 16.3 batching/parallelism is supported, with earlier 16.2 availability and feature-flag conditions. It concerns direct transfer, not a general task-archive performance guarantee.

sources.title: GitLab repository backup performance history
sources.inspected_scope: Git bundle duplicate-reference loop, benchmark and 18.0 availability
sources.independent_finding: The O(N²) reference loop and reported benchmark/release context are supported. They do not identify a bottleneck in this tracker.
